title: Models and performance
text: Don’t fork. ONNX Runtime’s thread pools don’t survive fork(), engine can’t used inside parallel::mclapply() future::multicore. layaR detects raises laya_error_forked error rather letting child process hang. One engine usually enough. single engine already spreads forward pass cores. Running several engines parallel machine mostly makes compete cores, multiplying memory use. Separate processes work. PSOCK workers (parallel::makePSOCKcluster(), future::multisession, callr), process loads engine. engine sent worker, saved saveRDS() read back, reconnects model folder first use, loads model process. useful across machines, intra_op_threads set workers share cores .

what: Batches: padding costs more than it saves on a CPU
title: Models and performance
text: forward pass can take several texts , every text padded longest one. GPU batching usually wins; CPU doesn’t. laya_predict_batch() therefore sends one text per forward pass default (batch_size = 1, layaR.batch_size option): answers whatever batch size; speed changes. run different hardware, try values batch_size sort_by_length = TRUE texts, set layaR.batch_size option best one. Even default batch size, laya_predict_batch() better tool many texts loop: checks questions , shows progress bar, stops cleanly interrupted. chunk_size decides often R gets control back ; doesn’t change throughput consistent way. differences run--run noise, size comes fastest changes one run next:
code: one_by_one <- function(x) for (s in x) laya_predict(s, qs, engine = engine) batch <- function(...) laya_predict_batch(texts[1:64], qs, engine = engine, progress = FALSE, ...) batches <- bench::mark(   `laya_predict() in a loop` = one_by_one(texts[1:64]),   `batch_size = 1 (default)` = batch(),   `batch_size = 4, sorted` = batch(batch_size = 4, sort_by_length = TRUE),   `batch_size = 16, sorted` = batch(batch_size = 16, sort_by_length = TRUE),   `whole chunk (NULL)` = batch(batch_size = NULL),   check = FALSE, min_iterations = 3, filter_gc = FALSE ) data.frame(method = as.character(batches$expression),            seconds = round(as.numeric(batches$median), 2),            texts_per_second = round(64 / as.numeric(batches$median), 1)) #>                     method seconds texts_per_second #> 1 laya_predict() in a loop   10.91              5.9 #> 2 batch_size = 1 (default)   10.88              5.9 #> 3   batch_size = 4, sorted   11.74              5.4 #> 4  batch_size = 16, sorted   14.79              4.3 #> 5       whole chunk (NULL)   19.33              3.3 chunks <- bench::mark(   `chunk_size = 16` = laya_predict_batch(texts, qs, engine = engine, chunk_size = 16,                                          progress = FALSE),   `chunk_size = 64` = laya_predict_batch(texts, qs, engine = engine, chunk_size = 64,                                          progress = FALSE),   `chunk_size = 256` = laya_predict_batch(texts, qs, engine = engine, chunk_size = 256,                                           progress = FALSE),   check = FALSE, min_iterations = 3, filter_gc = FALSE ) data.frame(method = as.character(chunks$expression),            texts_per_second = round(length(texts) / as.numeric(chunks$median), 1)) #>             method texts_per_second #> 1  chunk_size = 16              5.2 #> 2  chunk_size = 64              3.8 #> 3 chunk_size = 256              4.1 laya_engine_close(engine)

Results either way. sort_by_length Group similarly sized states within chunk reduce padding (batch_size 1 smaller chunk). chunk_size States sent engine per call. chunks R can interrupted progress bar updates. progress Show progress bar?
